explicit_validation.explanation: Paper validates LLM-as-judge against human evaluation specifically for utterance-level naturalness assessment, where both LLM (o1-preview) and humans distinguish between model-generated and human-rewritten utterances

prompts.notes: Full prompt shown in Appendix D (Figure D3) for distinguishing AI-generated vs human-rewritten utterances

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: relatively solid inter-rater consistency for human evaluations in Natural Language Generation tasks

guidelines.notes: Complete instructions provided to human validators in Appendix D (Figures D1, D2, D3) including rewriting guidelines and differentiation task instructions

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on subset of 117 utterance pairs where both human annotators correctly identified LLM-generated utterances

quantitative_scores.notes: LLM correctly distinguished 72 out of 117 pairs that humans had correctly identified
Human-human agreement on identifying LLM-generated utterances

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: 61.2% accuracy suggests LLMs find framework-generated utterances close to human writings

validation_results.summary_finding: o1-preview achieved 61.2% accuracy in distinguishing LLM-generated vs human-rewritten utterances on samples that humans had correctly identified, indicating that even for LLMs, utterances generated by the framework are close to human writings

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM primarily used for utterance-level quality assessment and perspective shift scoring, while humans conducted comprehensive dialogue-level evaluation including strategy analysis
